answer: Each grading task samples a quorum of graders at random from identities whose standing comes from years of accurate work and locked stake, so an attacker cannot know in advance who will judge; fake fresh identities win nothing because they are never drawn. To sway one verdict the attacker must corrupt many staked identities at once, and every exposed cheat slashes their stake and reputation, a ripple of losses. Costs stay cipher-hard to predict and grow like a glacier, slow and crushing, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
